title: Signal-to-inference boundary for early-stage company intelligence
author: Faye Niu
target_section: 2.2 Early-stage finance, portfolio reporting, and public company intelligence
purpose: Separate source-bound observations about funding, public support, Companies House records and reconstructed funding links from stronger company-quality, causal, valuation, ranking or investment conclusions that the admitted evidence does not support.

status.interpretation: Author synthesis of locally admitted literature and frozen project contracts; a reporting boundary rather than an empirical finding or decision model.

placement.purpose: Place LIT-T2 on one dedicated portrait page immediately after Section 2.2 and prevent Section 2.3 from preceding it when the exhibit is input at the approved chapter location.

row_traceability.boundary: Report only attributed event details and their source scope; do not convert a context-specific signal into firm quality, causality, forecast or investment merit.
Report the attributed award or support event and explicit coverage limits; do not infer causality, superiority, complete support history or realised impact.

row_traceability.evidence_class: Companies House identity or filing event
row_traceability.boundary: Use the exact company number and dated register fact without treating legal incorporation or filing presence as a complete operational, ownership or financial profile.
Describe a partial reconstruction under an explicit linkage rule while retaining unmatched gaps; do not claim an exhaustive history, causal pathway or forecast.

limitations: The exhibit synthesises literature and project contracts; it is not an empirical result from this artefact.
A source-bound event can be reported only to the extent supported by its admitted record, date, legal identity, locator and observation cutoff.
Crowdfunding findings remain platform-, country- and sample-dependent and do not define a universal company-quality signal.
Public grant and state-support associations can reflect selection or confounding and do not prove causal innovation, growth or performance effects.
Companies House records describe legal and filing facts at a dated register state, not a complete operational, ownership, private-funding or financial profile.
Cross-source funding reconstruction remains incomplete where identifiers, historical coverage or definitions differ; absence is not evidence of no event.
FCA guidance supports a conservative communication boundary but this exhibit is not legal advice.
The exhibit contains no mutable corpus count, evaluation result, company score, ranking, valuation, recommendation or investment-outcome claim.

self_hash_policy: The provenance file's own SHA-256 is reported externally because embedding it would create a self-referential hash.
